# center matrix M: rows B1..B4, cols C1..C4 (already in kernel)
# winner per line: rarest color among exactly-twice candidates; tie -> lower value
from collections import Counter
flat = Counter(v for row in M for v in row)
print("M =", M, "counts =", dict(flat))
def winner(seq):
    cnt = Counter(seq)
    cand = [c for c,n in cnt.items() if n == 2]
    if not cand: return None
    return sorted(cand, key=lambda c: (flat[c], c))[0]
out = [row[:] for row in G]
cells = []
for bi, r in enumerate(rows):
    w = winner(M[bi])
    idx = [i for i,v in enumerate(M[bi]) if v == w]
    for k in range(idx[0]+1, idx[1]+1):
        for gc in gap[k]:
            out[r][gc] = w; cells.append((r, gc, w))
for bj, c0 in enumerate(cols):
    seq = [M[b][bj] for b in range(4)]
    w = winner(seq)
    idx = [i for i,v in enumerate(seq) if v == w]
    for k in range(idx[0]+1, idx[1]+1):
        for gr in gap[k]:
            out[gr][c0] = w; cells.append((gr, c0, w))
print(len(cells), sorted(cells))
# sanity: reproduce demo1 conflict expectation (3 vs 1 tie -> 1) conceptually holds
import json; print(json.dumps(out))

def grids_from(t):
    # find "input (HxW):" then rows of numbers
    out=[]
    for m2 in re.finditer(r'(input|output) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n((?:[\d ]+\n?)+)', t):
        h,w=int(m2.group(2)),int(m2.group(3))
        rows=[[int(x) for x in ln.split()] for ln in m2.group(4).strip().split('\n')]
        assert len(rows)==h and all(len(r)==w for r in rows), (m2.group(1), h, len(rows))
        out.append((m2.group(1), rows))
    return out
